track: H2 — react-doctor main/shared/extensions, tool failure, and carry-over cleanup

sections.summary: Root cause of "maintainability checks failed / score not shown" found and proved: react-doctor enumerates files with `git ls-files -z --stage --others --exclude-standard`, which lists files still in git's index but deleted from the working tree. Wave 2's P22 deleted extensions/horus/src/warmup-clipboard.ts without staging it, so the maintainability/dead-code pass tried to open() it and threw. Machine-readable proof from --json: projects[0].skippedChecks == ["dead-code"], skippedCheckReasons["dead-code"] == "Maintainability analysis failed: Error: ENOENT ... warmup-clipboard.ts", summary.score == null. Confirmed by experiment (a 1-line placeholder at that path made the run print 81/100, deleting it restored the failure). Not scripts/**, not a parse error, not config. A doctor.config.jsonc with ignore.files does NOT help — the maintainability pass builds its file list before ignores are applied (tested; config removed, none committed). The only fix was a git index write, which this track is forbidden from doing, so it was measured around with scratchpad/rd.sh (copies .git/index, removes that one entry from the copy, runs react-doctor with GIT_INDEX_FILE pointed at it; the repo's index untouched) — that printed 81/100 at the time. The deletion has since been staged (not by this track), git ls-files no longer reports it, and a plain `npx react-doctor@latest` now prints the score. No repo file changed for this section.
sections.gates: react-doctor score printed: 81/100 via scratchpad/rd.sh at diagnosis time; 87/100 from a plain run now that the index is clean. No edits, so lint/typecheck not re-run for this section.
sections.deviations: Fix was an owner action (git index write) rather than a source change; documented as needs-owner and then resolved externally mid-run. Also worth reporting upstream: react-doctor should skip ENOENT files in the maintainability pass instead of dropping the whole check and the score, and the CLI never prints the reason (only --json exposes skippedCheckReasons).

sections.summary: folderIndex.ts async-await-in-loop x4 (:47 :50 :56 :150) and server-sequential-independent-await (:81) all cleared with real concurrency, no disable comments. collectFolderCandidates now resolves the six default-scan-root probes and every remembered-root probe in one Promise.all round (resolveScanRoot runs its stat and realpath together; they never needed each other). walk() collects its children's realpath + .git probe into one Promise.all — a directory of 40 children went from 80 serial syscalls to a single round. A new visitInOrder(items, visit) promise chain replaces both genuinely sequential for-await loops (scan roots, and the depth-first descent), because the MAX_FOLDERS cap makes order load-bearing; sequencing is now structure shared by both call sites rather than a comment repeated twice. resolveOpenableFolder resolves the home realpath and the approved-root realpaths together; error precedence unchanged. Equivalence proved rather than assumed: a verbatim copy of the old algorithm in the scratchpad, run against the real $HOME plus a directory, a missing path and a file as remembered roots, gave 103 vs 103 candidates with JSON.stringify identical on every round, at 14.8-15.3 ms before vs 9.1-10.2 ms after.

sections.deviations: An intermediate entries.filter().map() tripped js-combine-iterations and was folded into a single loop. Spent time probing why the rule fires here but not on the identical-looking loop in ignoredListing.ts: it only fires in TS/TSX (a .mjs copy is silent) and skips a loop whose body itself mutates the accumulator the guard reads — a verbatim copy of ignoredListing.ts scans clean, so there was no shape to imitate.

sections.summary: extensions/horus/src/open-pull-request.tsx no-set-state-after-await-in-effect x2 cleared. The rule is inter-procedural — it follows local helpers out of the effect — so a first attempt that checked an AbortSignal inside warmup/openUrl still reported both effects; the post-await setters had to move into the effects behind a visible cancelled flag with a cleanup. The single [incoming] effect became two (launch-argument open, clipboard read), each returning a cleanup, and the clipboard .then now drops a superseded read instead of writing clipboardUrl over a newer one. Warmup became one effect keyed on the derived candidate (typed ?? clipboardUrl) instead of a call in each of the two old effects; claimWarmup still dedupes per URL so coverage is unchanged, the failure path always releases the claim (URL stays retryable) and only the badge write is gated on cancelled. openUrl was split: the state-free part (deliver) hoisted to module scope, openUrl left as the action-panel path, warmUrl added for the action-panel warmup.

sections.summary: All five Wave 3 carries landed. W3-X1: new exported pullRequestReviewLane(intent) plus a lane parameter on runGitHubReadCommand (forwarded to runCommand — the retry loop is the one place a lane could be dropped), threaded from getPullRequestReview through #loadPullRequestReview, #revalidateCachedPullRequestReview, #fetchPullRequestReview, #loadPullRequestChecks, #emitPullRequestChecks, #collectPullRequestDiff, #collectPullRequestPatchFromFilesApi, #resolvePullRequestIdentity and #getGitHubViewerLogin, so warmup gh hops run on the background lane. W3-X2: named "no vendor-shiki engine chunk in the pre-mount closure" assertion in check-entry-chunk.mjs next to the WorkerPool check, backed by a new closureChunksInGroup helper (Rollup hashes contain hyphens, so a group cannot be read off the last segment). W3-X4: RepositoryService.open(folderPath, resolved = false) with repositorySessions passing true, removing the last redundant realpath. W3-X3: startup-probe now reports paletteOpenAppMs read from the horus:palette-open-to-focus measure, in the per-sample block, the medians and the PERF summary line. W3-X5: emptyRows now goes through a new stableReading() in cdp.mjs that polls until two consecutive counts agree or a 100 ms settle window is up, so the staged 12-then-the-rest rows are not misread; nulls never count as settled. scripts/perf/README.md documents both.

reviewNotes:
1. **vendor-shiki-langs is in the pre-mount closure** (found while wiring W3-X2, not fixed). A plain `vendor-shiki` prefix assertion FAILS against the current build: `vendor-shiki-langs-ByDSOINb.js` (31 KB) is statically imported by `vendor-diffs`, which DiffSurface / MultiFileReview / WorkspaceRoot pull in. The engine itself (`vendor-shiki-BEzecXZ0.js`, 143 KB) is NOT — it appears only in a `vite__mapDeps` dynamic list, so P31 holds. `vendor-shiki-langs` is the lazy-language table rather than grammars, so the assertion is scoped to the engine and the exclusion is documented in the script. Worth a decision if you want the last 31 KB off the pre-mount path.

2. **Lane on a joined flight (W3-X1 limit).** A foreground reader that joins an in-flight warmup inherits the background lane, because the gh hops are already queued when it joins. Promoting a running flight needs the semaphore to support re-laning; out of scope for a cleanup carry, called out rather than silently accepted.

3. **The missing score was hiding project-level rules.** With the maintainability pass finally completing, `duplicate-jsx-subtree` went from 1 site to 7. Part of that is H1's in-flight component splits, but the project-level rules were invisible while the pass was failing — whoever closes P13 at 100/100 should expect findings that were never in the 30-warning baseline. All are in src/renderer.

4. **react-doctor rule quirks worth knowing for the rest of P13.** `async-await-in-loop` only fires in TS/TSX (a `.mjs` copy of the same code is silent) and skips a loop whose body itself mutates the accumulator the guard reads — which is why `ignoredListing.ts` scans clean with the same shape. `no-set-state-after-await-in-effect` is inter-procedural: a guard inside a local helper does not satisfy it, the guarded setter has to be inside the effect. `ignore.files` in a config does not affect the maintainability pass's file list.

5. **The Raycast extension has no node_modules**, so `npx ray lint` and its tsc cannot run here; the 4 errors tsc does report are all consequences of the missing `@raycast/api` and are identical before and after my change. Someone with the install should re-lint `extensions/horus` before shipping.

6. **scratchpad/rd.sh is left in place** — it measures react-doctor around a stale index entry without touching `.git/index`. Not needed now that the deletion is staged, but it is the tool for this failure mode if an unstaged deletion turns up again.
